what_slowed_me_down: The context.dev /web/scrape/markdown endpoint itself was fast and reliable (all 40 pages scraped successfully, ~5s each, $0.002/page), and the markdown was clean enough to extract plan names and prices. What slowed me down: (1) Initial global npm install of the CLI failed with EACCES, so I had to set up a user-local npm prefix before `monid` was available. (2) The endpoint takes the target URL as a query param rather than in the body, which I only learned from `monid inspect` — fine, but an extra step. (3) The real time sink was not Monid but the extraction work: every pricing page structures plans differently (monthly vs annual toggles, per-seat vs flat, struck-through monthly prices next to annual prices, yearly totals that needed dividing by 12, 'starts at' usage-based pricing), so each of the 40 markdown files needed manual reading and judgment. (4) One page (semrush.com/prices) redirected to a different pricing URL, and a few pages bury the plan cards under very long navigation menus in the markdown. Overall Monid did its job well; the normalization task on top was the slow part.
